currents.modelsDetailValueNote: Value score = geometric mean of the overall-ability percentile and the inverted-cost percentile; standard cost assumes 1M input + 0.25M output tokens.

currents.modelsMethSubtitle: Data sources, inclusion rules, and the scoring & confidence formulas are fully public; parameters are frozen per version and any change bumps the version.
currents.modelsMethRuleInclusion: Verified released foundation models appear on one default board, including those without evaluations or pricing. Vendor-official previews have a separate view; rumors and unannounced models are excluded. Each foundation model occupies one row, with configurations and snapshots in its details. Unknown names require identity verification, not fuzzy automatic merging.
currents.modelsMethRuleScoring: Each source's scores are first converted to tie-aware 0–100 percentiles within that source. When a source lists multiple configurations, the source-designated default is used if available, otherwise the median — never the best configuration. Multiple boards run by the same operator are averaged within the group first, then independent operators are combined with equal weight. A missing source never counts as zero (it does not directly lower ability); it only reduces confidence.
currents.modelsMethRuleConfidence: Confidence combines coverage (45%), freshness (25%), agreement (25%), and identity mapping (5%), independently of ability. Limited coverage does not exclude a model. Without usable evaluations, ability, confidence, and rank display —.
currents.modelsMethRuleValue: Every included model remains visible. Comparable prices use official USD global or international standard online, uncached, ordinary-context rates; time-of-day pricing uses the peak rate. The aggregate usage basket is 1M input + 0.25M output tokens. Value is the geometric mean of ability percentile and inverted-cost percentile. Non-USD rates retain their original currency without FX conversion. Unknown prices, subscriptions, self-hosting, and non-comparable plans are not scored and display —.
currents.modelsMethRuleFailure: Failed assessment sources retain their last valid snapshot. If all assessments fail, no new ability scores are published. Unchanged scores do not advance the score-change clock; history retains one effective point per day. Prices are checked independently. Failures preserve the last valid quote and its actual verification date, never extending a promotion. Price changes update value only, not ability scores or ability history. Newly listed models show no rank movement.

lab.label: Experiments
lab.title: Lab
lab.subtitle: Interactive experiments built from first principles — WebGL shaders, physics engines, algorithm visualizations. All hand-written, zero dependencies.
lab.metaDescription: Twelve interactive experiments written from scratch — WebGL shaders, physics, flow fields, algorithm visualization, zero dependencies. Every demo keeps a readable still and description with 3D off.
lab.webglUnavailable: WebGL unavailable on this device, showing static preview

particles.title: Particle System
particles.desc: Real-time particle simulation: thousands of particles with mouse repulsion and 3D drift, all on the GPU.
particles.layer: The GPU update step and mouse repulsion are hand-written. No Three.js.
particles.stillAlt: Blue, violet and white particles distributed on a dark canvas.

shader.title: Shader Mixer
shader.desc: Live GLSL noise art: drag sliders to tune hue, flow speed and turbulence octaves — every frame computed in real time.
shader.layer: The FBM noise fragment shader and uniform binding are hand-written.
shader.stillAlt: Violet and pink noise patterns forming curling streams.

fluid.title: Fluid Simulation
fluid.desc: Hand-written Navier-Stokes solver: ping-pong FBO, vorticity confinement, Jacobi pressure iterations — drag to inject velocity & dye.
fluid.layer: The full fluid pipeline is hand-written. No off-the-shelf fluid library.
fluid.stillAlt: Blue and violet dye curling and diffusing through a velocity field on a dark canvas.

physics.title: Physics Sandbox
physics.desc: Verlet integration + spatial hash collision: click to spawn balls, drag to throw, gravity toggle, elastic collisions.
physics.layer: The integrator and broad-phase collision are hand-written. No physics engine.
physics.stillAlt: Five colored balls resting against the sandbox floor.

flow.title: Flow Field Particles
flow.desc: Curl noise divergence-free flow: 2500 particles with long trails, mouse attract/repel toggle.
flow.layer: The curl-noise field and trail integration are hand-written. No particle library.
flow.stillAlt: Blue particles tracing curved flow lines with continuous trails.

morph.title: 3D Morph
morph.desc: Parametric surface per-point morph: sphere→torus→cube→wave, drag to rotate, auto-cycle.
morph.layer: The parametric surface and per-vertex morph are hand-written. No model files.
morph.stillAlt: Blue-violet particles forming an undulating parametric surface.

sdf.title: SDF Raymarching
sdf.desc: Combine and subtract sphere, box and torus distance fields, then adjust shape, lighting and material to explore soft shadows and reflections.
sdf.layer: Distance functions, ray marching, normal estimation, soft shadows and a single reflection bounce are implemented directly in GLSL, without a 3D engine.
sdf.stillAlt: A union of sphere and box distance fields with shadows and reflections.

cloth.title: Tearable Cloth
cloth.desc: Drag, cut or pin cloth nodes, adjust wind and toggle a circular obstacle to see how mesh constraints hold the fabric together.
cloth.layer: Verlet integration, XPBD distance constraints, cutting and obstacle collision are implemented in local algorithms, with simulation running in a Web Worker.
cloth.stillAlt: A pinned cloth mesh above a spherical obstacle.

pathfinding.title: Pathfinding
pathfinding.desc: Compare A* and Dijkstra visitation order and shortest paths on the same editable obstacle map, with playback and single-step controls.
pathfinding.layer: Frontier selection, the Manhattan heuristic, distance updates and path reconstruction are implemented directly on a shared four-neighbor, unit-cost grid.
pathfinding.stillAlt: A* and Dijkstra results on the same obstacle map.

raft.title: Raft Consensus
raft.desc: Explore elections, log replication and majority commits in a five-node simulation; stop nodes or partition the network to inspect state changes.
raft.layer: Voting, term comparison, log-conflict backtracking and majority-commit rules are implemented directly in deterministic rounds, not a live distributed network.
raft.stillAlt: Five nodes showing election, log replication and majority commits.

audio.title: Sound & Spectrum
audio.desc: Switch oscillator waveforms and adjust frequency, gain and low-pass cutoff while viewing the waveform and spectrum. Sound starts only when you press Play.
audio.layer: Audio-node wiring, parameter controls and visualization are implemented in the component; oscillation, filtering and spectral analysis use the browser's native Web Audio API.
audio.stillAlt: A silent time-domain baseline and empty frequency spectrum.

geometry.title: Voronoi / Delaunay
geometry.desc: Add, move or remove sample points to see Voronoi regions and the Delaunay triangulation update with the point set.
geometry.layer: Bowyer–Watson triangulation and equidistant half-plane clipping are implemented directly to generate the triangle mesh and bounded Voronoi regions.
geometry.stillAlt: Voronoi regions and a Delaunay triangulation of sample points.

agent.title: Agent Access
agent.heading: Let your Agent use Currents directly
agent.subtitle: Over MCP and an Agent Skill, your agent can query current AI hot events, search reports, read multi-source event timelines, and fetch the Currents Daily — bilingual, read-only, and never mutating site data.
agent.layerMcpDesc: Five read-only tools exposed over the MCP protocol: hot board, search, report detail, event timeline, and daily digest. Credentials are issued individually after an invite.
agent.layerSkillDesc: The Skill teaches the agent when to use which tool and how to preserve event confidence and the Watching-board distinction. MCP provides capability; the Skill keeps it correct — together they are Currents Agent Access.
agent.example2: Find the latest Currents reports about agents.
agent.example4: Which independent sources cover this event, and how did its heat change?
agent.toolHotDesc: The current event board: a high-confidence main board plus a Watching section, narrowable to news, products, or research.
agent.toolSearchDesc: Full-text search over published reports by topic, organization, model, or phrase.
agent.toolItemDesc: Read one report: score context, translations, and source links.
agent.toolEventDesc: Read a multi-source event: timeline, confidence, lifecycle, heat history, and merge lineage.
agent.toolDailyDesc: Fetch the latest Currents Daily or an exact-date archive.
agent.mcpIntro: With your invited credentials, add the MCP endpoint to your client configuration. Replace placeholders such as TOKEN with the issued values.
agent.mcpEndpointNote: Endpoint: POST {endpoint} with header Authorization: Bearer TOKEN.
agent.skillIntro: Load the Skill in the client that uses the MCP server, so the agent learns Currents query strategy and event semantics.
agent.skillStep1: Get the Skill package (attached to the invite email, or via the agreed path).
agent.skillStep2: Place SKILL.md in your client's skill directory (e.g. ~/.codex/skills/currents/ for Codex).
agent.skillStep3: Start a new session — Skills load at session start; an already-open session won't pick it up.
agent.verifyIntro: After configuring, open a new session and verify in order:
agent.verifyStep1: Ask "What's hot in AI today?" — the agent should call currents_hot and keep main board vs. Watching distinct.
agent.verifyStep2: Ask about a specific topic — the agent should call currents_search, then follow up with currents_item or currents_event by ID.
agent.verifyStep3: Ask for today's daily summary — the agent should call currents_daily.
agent.verifySuccess: Success criteria: all five tools are discoverable and callable; answers preserve confidence and Watching semantics; configuration survives a client restart.
agent.trouble1Desc: Confirm you edited the file your client actually reads, then fully restarted the client (not just a new window).
agent.trouble2Desc: The credential is missing, mistyped, or in the wrong place. Check the Authorization: Bearer TOKEN header against the invite email.
agent.trouble3Desc: Skills load at session start — open a new session after installing, and confirm SKILL.md sits in the client's expected skill directory.
agent.trouble4Desc: It was written to a transient session instead of the persistent config file. Re-add it at the persistent location shown above.
agent.inviteDesc: Access is invite-only for now: reach out through the site's public contact channel, mention your client and use case — no other personal information needed.
